title: LLM route/release/deploy/approval/rollback control plane
description: Reconstructed PSTF slice for Bahia's LLM control plane. This slice covers LLM route creation, release registration, signer-first deployment and approval flows, reconcile-driven route state publication, rollback as a first-class action, and the approved intent that this capability should be available through a full end-user web workflow.
dependencies: `/api/v1/system/info` feature-gated advertisement of LLM request/result/read-model kinds
Bahia signer-first Nostr request/result transport for kinds 5971-5975, 6973, and 7971-7973
shared web control-plane store consumption of Bahia-signed read models and activity events
future dedicated web route/page workflow approved by HITL-LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT-001

summary: Bahia advertises LLM request/result/read-model kinds from `/api/v1/system/info` only when the LLM feature is enabled.
The reactor handles signed Nostr requests for route create (5971), release register (5972), deploy (5973), approval/reject (5974), and rollback (5975).

Route create and release register publish immediate terminal results (7971, 7972). Deploy and rollback publish an initial 6973 status reply with `status=processing` and step `accepted`, then background provisioning emits additional 6973 progress and a terminal 7973 result through `LLMResponder`.

The web app currently consumes LLM route and route-state read models through the shared control-plane store and activity feed, but selected evidence shows no dedicated LLM route/page under `web/src/routes`.

REST read routes for LLM entities are mounted when `LLMRegistry` exists; route create/update and release create are also mounted in the primary write group; a second operational REST mutation surface exists behind `cfg.LLM.AllowOperationalREST` and operator auth.

Current rollback code scans recent deployed intents, picks the first previously deployed release that differs from the current desired release, and records `SupersedesIntentID` from the latest deployed intent it encounters.
A full end-user web workflow is intended now for this feature slice, not merely API/MCP/operator-only behavior.
Canonical behavior is signer-first and event-driven: publish signed LLM request events, subscribe for correlated 6973/797x replies, and consume 31964/31965 read models for browser state.
The flagged operational REST mutation endpoints are not part of the approved intended product contract.
Rollback remains a first-class user-visible action, but the current target-selection/supersedence algorithm is not approved and must be changed before rollback semantics can be treated as normative.

happy_paths.title: Create an LLM route and register a release
steps: A signed request creates a route and receives 7971 `LLMRouteCreateResult` with the new `route_id`.
A signed request registers a release for that route and receives 7972 `LLMReleaseRegisterResult` with `route_id` and `release_id`.
Bahia projects 31964 `LLMRouteRegistry` for browser-visible route state.

happy_paths.title: Deploy an LLM release to an environment
steps: A signed 5973 request includes explicit `route`, `environment`, and `release` correlation tags.
The reactor validates the request, creates a deployment intent, and publishes 6973 with `status=processing` and step `accepted`.
The provisioning coordinator emits additional 6973 progress for backend placement, provisioning, gate evaluation, gateway sync, and observation recording.
On success, Bahia publishes terminal 7973 and updates 31965 `LLMRouteState` so browser-visible state reflects the deployed release and synced gateway/backend state.

happy_paths.title: Approve or reject a protected-environment deployment intent
steps: A protected-environment deploy request creates a pending LLM deployment intent.
A signed 5974 request with decision `approve` or `reject` targets the intent by content or `intent` tag.
Bahia publishes terminal 7973 describing the recorded decision.
If rejected, route state is repaired away from the rejected desired intent; if approved, downstream provisioning may continue and later produce 6973/7973 lifecycle replies.

failure_paths.title: Unauthorized or unavailable LLM request
failure_paths.behavior: If the requester pubkey is not authorized or the LLM registry is unavailable, the reactor publishes a correlated error result instead of silently accepting the request.

failure_paths.title: Malformed or invalid request payload
failure_paths.behavior: Malformed JSON, invalid UUIDs, or an invalid approval decision produce correlated error results with validation or parse failure steps.

failure_paths.title: No relay accepted the signed deploy or rollback request
failure_paths.behavior: The command publisher fails before acceptance if zero relays accept the request; no false success is returned.

failure_paths.title: Provisioning, promotion gate, or gateway sync failure
failure_paths.behavior: Background deployment failures complete the run as failed, emit terminal 7973 error replies, and leave route state drifted or error-marked rather than reporting success.

non_functional_requirements: LLM control-plane interactions must remain event-driven and subscription-based; request completion must not depend on polling or arbitrary sleep-based waits.
Correlation must stay explicit via `e`, `p`, `route`, `environment`, `release`, `intent`, and when applicable `run` tags.
Browser-visible LLM state must come from Bahia-signed replaceable read models and correlated lifecycle events, with latest-wins replaceable handling and EOSE-aware bootstrap/live handoff.
Deploy and rollback request acceptance (6973 `accepted`) must not be misclassified as terminal success; terminal outcome is the later 7973 reply from the asynchronous deployment path.
Current approved intended behavior should not depend on the flagged operational REST mutation surface.

contradictions.note: `docs/api.md` omits the mounted LLM HTTP routes entirely, while router and handlers implement them.
HITL approved a full end-user web workflow as intended now, but selected route evidence shows no dedicated LLM page or browser workflow under `web/src/routes`.

Current rollback selection and supersedence behavior is observable in code, but HITL classified it as needing change rather than preservation.

open_questions.question: What explicit rollback target-selection and supersedence rule should replace the current implicit scan for a previous deployed release?
open_questions.reason: HITL classified the current rollback rule as FIX, but no replacement behavior was approved.
open_questions.blocking_scope: Rollback acceptance criteria and final intended rollback behavior

evidence_gaps: Selected evidence proves backend, transport, projection, and shared-store behavior, but not a current end-to-end browser workflow for LLM route/release/deploy/approval/rollback.
Selected tests do not yet prove approval-to-provisioning browser journeys or rollback browser journeys.
Rollback semantics are intentionally left non-normative until a replacement rule is approved.
